answer: Pairs of graders with 30+ shared rows are tested: how often both stood with, or both against, the verdict, versus what their own pass rates imply. In E29-E39 Voyage, Pearl and Lantern matched on 86/86, 60/60 and 52/52 rows where chance expects 59, 62 and 64 %; each outcome has odds below 1 in 10^10. Pairs under 1 in 100,000 merge into one cluster holding a single seat per panel. Cheapest bypass: dissent on rows the ring wins anyway, which costs no power; splitting a ring over 20 accounts also keeps each pair under 30 rows. Honest same-model graders can false-flag.
